before: reduce turns a sequence into one result by repeatedly combining the result so far with the next element. The initial accumulator is already a real result: an empty sequence returns it unchanged.

joinedLabels takes labels plus a prefix. labels.reduce(prefix) starts the accumulated String at prefix. Each closure call receives that string and one label, then returns a new string with the label in brackets. + concatenates strings here; it is not integer addition. The next call receives the returned accumulator. reduce does not mutate labels or prefix, and source order matters for this string-building operation.

```swift
func joinedLabels(_ labels: [String], startingWith prefix: String) -> String {
    return labels.reduce(prefix) { accumulated, label in
        accumulated + "[" + label + "]"
    }
}
print(joinedLabels(["map", "notes"], startingWith: "Trip:"))
```
Expected output:
```text
Trip:[map][notes]
```

after: `reduce` combines a sequence into one result. You give it a starting value and a closure that combines the current result with the next item.
The result so far is called the accumulator. Each closure call receives it and the next label, then returns the updated result. In this example, `+` joins text rather than adding numbers.
With an empty list, the closure never runs, so reduce returns the starting value unchanged. That starting value also matters for nonempty lists; it is not only a fallback.
